source_text: Argui ergo, et iure argui, deiectam et debilem varietatem, qua fuerat effectum ut et nuptias te non damnare praemitteres, et diceres, ob viri et feminae commixtionem, quam de nuptiarum conditione et natura venire perspicuum est, immo in qua sola (quantum ad conflictum nostrum respicit) nuptiarum veritas est, homines in diaboli iura transcribi.
pass_a_gloss: I was therefore argued, and rightly argued, a cast-down and weak variety, by which it had been effected that both you would send ahead that you do not condemn marriages, and you would say that, on account of the mingling of man and woman, which it is perspicuous comes from the condition and nature of marriages, nay in which alone (as much as looks to our conflict) the truth of marriages is, humans are transcribed into the rights of the devil.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: I criticized, and rightly criticized, your abject and feeble inconsistency. It led you first to say that you did not condemn marriage, and then to say that human beings are transferred into the devil's legal possession because of the union of man and woman. That union plainly belongs to marriage's condition and nature; indeed, as far as our present dispute is concerned, in that alone lies the reality of marriage.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
